answer: Latency-shadow enrollment. Each new agent identity must complete a timed round-trip through a randomly assigned, low-traffic relay island before gaining standing; the route is chosen from live network state and never repeats, so the answer cannot be copied or precomputed. An attacker cannot reuse a solved path and must hold real presence at the route's zenith, paying fresh infrastructure, distinct IP space, and idle wait time per identity—costs that scale linearly with every sybil while remaining trivial for honest agents, since genuine traffic already traverses the ocean of relays.
